plan: With a private value of $31, I want to win if possible, but not overpay. Other bidders have values randomly drawn between $0-$49. A pure Nash equilibrium strategy suggests bidding slightly below my true value. Given the random distribution, I'll bid strategically around $25-$30 to maximize potential profit. This gives me buffer room to win without overpaying, assuming other rational bidders will also bid strategically below their true value.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction with values between $0-$49, the optimal strategy is typically to bid close to, but slightly below, my true value. With a $37 value, rational opponents will likely bid near their own values. I want to win if my value is higher, but avoid overpaying. A bid around $36-$36.5 seems strategic - high enough to likely win if I have a top value, but not risking overpaying by bidding my full $37.

In a second-price sealed bid auction with values between $0-$49, the optimal strategy is to bid close to my true value. My value is $11. Other bidders are also rational.
